transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Chen (Redwood AE), Riley Ortiz (Redwood SE), Marisol Vega (Redwood CSM), Dana Rousseau (Aureon Head Procurement), Priya Malhotra (Aureon CISO), Jonah Lee (Aureon ML Platform), Hector Alvarez (Aureon Legal)

Auto-summary (auto gen - may be noisy):
Redwood walked through contract path and SLA matrix. Customer flagged three must-haves: local EU data residency, KMS-managed keys with customer control, and explicit latency SLO with credits. Redwood proposed pilot with dedicated capacity and fallback to hosted variants. Action: pricing and legal artifacts to follow.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, appreciate you carving time. Quick intros and then we can jump to the MSA redline items.
[00:20] Dana Rousseau: Hi, this is Dana from Aureon — thanks. We're just hoping to get clarity today on what you'll accept and where we need exceptions. We've got a little procurement window open for October.
[00:31] Ethan Chen: Great, yeah, our goal is to get you a clean path to pilot — Riley, you wanna kick to the tech and SLA bits?
[00:37] Riley Ortiz: Sure. Hey all, I'm Riley, SE on the account. Quick note on our deployment options: we support a hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private VPC/on-prem deployments. Each has different controls for keys, data flow, and SLAs.
[01:00] Priya Malhotra: For us, the priority is data residency for EU customers and customer-managed keys. We need to be able to prove to auditors that the customer retains control of keys. Does Redwood support HSM or BYOK?
[01:18] Riley Ortiz: Yes, we do both. For hosted we offer a KMS integration where you can bring your own key via supported cloud KMS; for private deployments we support HSM integrations and the key material never leaves your control plane. Small caveat: hosted tier with BYOK increases onboarding time and has a small performance variance.
[01:38] Jonah Lee: Can you be specific about the variance? We need to model for 150ms p90 inference on typical prompts, so I need numbers to feed into capacity planning.
[01:50] Riley Ortiz: Totally. On hosted with BYOK, we typically see a 5-8% token latency bump due to crypto unwrap on the hot path; for dedicated capacity that's negligible. For private/on-prem where keys are local it's effectively zero. Those are ballpark. We'll run a baseline with your prompts to get exacts.
[02:10] Hector Alvarez: On legal, our DPA lists a 30-day deletion requirement for customer-generated data and a 90-day audit log retention window. What flexibility do you have?
[02:21] Ethan Chen: We're usually OK with 30-day deletion, but it depends — e.g., logs used for billing and fraud detection we often hold longer by default; we can narrow scope in the DPA.
[02:33] Marisol Vega: We can set scoped retention buckets — production logs vs metrics vs audit — and propose deletion APIs. We also have an export workflow for you.
[02:44] Hector Alvarez: Good. Also need to confirm egress paths for EU workloads — we can't have model inference cross to US regions for processing.
[02:54] Riley Ortiz: We can pin region routing policies and guarantee processing within eu-west-1 or other EU regions. For hosted, we have controls to route by policy. For dedicated or private it's even stricter.
[03:06] Dana Rousseau: Sounds doable. Another ask: SLA credits. Your SLA doc has a 99.5% uptime and latency SLO for API, but it doesn't say how credits are calculated for token-level latency misses. How do you remediate?
[03:22] Ethan Chen: Great question. Our standard SLA has availability credits for downtime. For latency SLOs, we usually offer an objective with operational remediation — e.g., a service credit if p90 exceeds target over a rolling week and we fail canary fallbacks. For enterprise contracts we can translate latency misses to defined credits. We'll need to map to agreed measurement points — client side vs edge.
[03:42] Priya Malhotra: Measurement points matter. We will require server-side measurements with tracing headers, not client-side measurements that we can't audit.
[03:51] Riley Ortiz: That's fine. We can provide server-side traces and token-level timing. Our console exposes per-route p50/p90/p99 and token breakdowns — and we can grant read-only log access for auditors.
[04:06] Jonah Lee: There was also a comment in the procurement binder about fallback behavior if your dedicated pool hits capacity — do you automatically route to hosted, or do you block? We need predictable behavior.
[04:17] Ethan Chen: We can configure routing policies. Default enterprise behavior is to fallback to a compatible model variant in another region or our hosted pool if you allow it; otherwise we can queue or rate-limit. That behavior is part of the rollout policy in the contract.
[04:33] Dana Rousseau: We prefer no unexpected cross-region fallback without manual approval.
[04:38] Ethan Chen: Understood — we can set policy to require manual approval for fallback or only allow it for non-production routes.
[04:45] Hector Alvarez: Back to the MSA redlines — indemnity and IP carve-outs. There are two items we typically ask: 1) limit on liability at the level of fees paid, and 2) an assurance about models not being used for training on customer data. Can you commit to a no-training clause?
[05:03] Ethan Chen: Yes, Redwood's standard position is we do not use customer prompt data to train public models. We can put that in the DPA/MPF (model processing framework) clause. For liability limits we generally negotiate on enterprise deals, we can take that to legal and propose a cap linked to the contract value.
[05:21] Hector Alvarez: Great. Please mark that in the redline.
[05:25] Riley Ortiz: Quick technical note — regarding no-training, we also have an option to run a private model variant which is fully isolated and cannot be used in our training pipeline at all. That might be useful if you want extra assurance.
[05:38] Priya Malhotra: That would help. For the pilot, can we do dedicated reserved capacity in EU with customer-managed KMS?
[05:46] Ethan Chen: Yes, pilot can be dedicated EU capacity + BYOK. Pricing will reflect that. We'll provide rates for a 6-week pilot and a committed capacity option if you decide to move to production.
[05:58] Dana Rousseau: On pricing, here's where procurement will push back — we need to see a model for committed vs burst pricing and a clawback if utilization is low.
[06:08] Ethan Chen: We can provide a sliding scale: committed base rate with a utilization credit model — if you commit to X tokens and use less, some credit applies, whereas burst is billed at a higher unit. We'll surface a sample workbook.
[06:19] Jonah Lee: For the baseline run, what inputs do you need from us? We'll provide a 5000-prompt set representative of our traffic. Any specific format?
[06:27] Riley Ortiz: JSONL with prompt / expected tokens / concurrency pattern works. Also tell us target latency constraints and any real-time timeouts. We'll spin up a dedicated small cluster and run a 48-hour baseline and send back p50/p90/p99 and cost estimates.
[06:41] Hector Alvarez: Security — we need SOC 2 Type II report and penetration test summary. Also want to understand how Redwood handles third-party subprocessors.
[06:52] Marisol Vega: We can provide SOC 2, ISO summary, and a subprocessors list. For penetration tests, we have a summary report and we can redacted details. Subprocessors are disclosed in the DPA and we support subprocessors with standard contract flow.
[07:04] Priya Malhotra: What about data exfil protection - do you do ML-specific filters to prevent leakage of PII in responses?
[07:13] Riley Ortiz: We have data-classification hooks and optional response filters. For highly regulated flows we recommend private deployment where we can narrow tokenizer vocab and output policies. In the hosted world we offer content filters and custom sanitizers.
[07:27] Ethan Chen: Also worth noting we can set up a proxy that supervises responses and strips PII before it returns — that's part of the integration patterns we've used for finance customers.
[07:37] Dana Rousseau: Good. Procurement will want an explicit section in the MSA about audit rights and on-site audits — is that something you entertain?
[07:46] Hector Alvarez: We usually ask for one on-site or virtual audit per year.
[07:50] Ethan Chen: We do virtual audits; on-site can be evaluated but often we provide attestation, SOC 2, and evidence. We can create a path in the contract with an agreed scope for remote auditing.
[08:02] Jonah Lee: Let's talk about rollback behavior during canary deploys and model rollouts; if a new model variant increases hallucination rates, how do we trigger an automatic rollback?
[08:12] Riley Ortiz: We support automated rollback policies tied to quality regressions — you can provide evaluation prompts and thresholds. If the evaluation fails a threshold we can auto-roll back and notify. These eval hooks are configurable per-route.
[08:24] Priya Malhotra: Will those evals be part of the pilot? We want to ensure regression monitoring before full rollout.
[08:29] Marisol Vega: Yes, we'll include a quality monitoring baseline in the pilot deliverable and set up alerts in the console.
[08:39] Dana Rousseau: On the contract timeline, procurement wants to close by end of October. Is that feasible?
[08:44] Ethan Chen: It's tight but doable. Steps: we share redlines this week, run baseline mid-September, negotiate MSA/DPA in the week after, then finalize pricing and signatures by late October. The gating items are legal exceptions and procurement approval cycles.
[08:58] Hector Alvarez: Speaking of exceptions, we will have a few DPA carve-outs about audit log retention and subprocessors in non-EU regions. We'll send a prioritized list.
[09:07] Ethan Chen: Perfect — Hector, if you send that prioritized list we'll put together a response matrix.
[09:12] Hector Alvarez: Will do.
[09:15] Riley Ortiz: Quick tech question from my side — Jonah, what is your expected concurrency distribution? That affects queueing and batching.
[09:22] Jonah Lee: Typical spikes ~200 concurrent requests, baseline 40 qps, average 26 tokens per request. We'll include histograms.
[09:30] Riley Ortiz: Great, that helps. We'll size and provide cost per 1M tokens in that pattern.
[09:36] Dana Rousseau: Also, procurement wants a termination clause tied to unsatisfactory SLAs with a 60-day cure period. Is that standard?
[09:45] Ethan Chen: We can include a termination-for-cause with cure period; 60 days is within typical negotiation range. We'll flag that.
[09:53] Priya Malhotra: Any details on encryption at rest for embeddings store? We need per-customer namespaces and encryption keys.
[10:02] Riley Ortiz: We encrypt at rest and support per-tenant namespaces. For embeddings we can enable envelope encryption with your KMS keys.
[10:11] Jonah Lee: For the pilot we need a dedicated embeddings store in EU.
[10:15] Riley Ortiz: Noted — we'll include that in the baseline.
[10:19] Dana Rousseau: One procedural thing — procurement requires a point-of-contact for billing disputes and a billing SLA. Who's that on Redwood's side?
[10:27] Marisol Vega: That's me — Marisol, CSM. I'll be your billing POC and will handle dispute triage with finance. We'll add billing SLA language to the pricing workbook.
[10:37] Hector Alvarez: Back to legal, we may ask for a data processing addendum that references local EU data protection representatives; do you have local DPO contacts?
[10:47] Ethan Chen: We can provide a DPO contact and localized DPA language referencing EU rep. We'll add that to the documentation bundle.
[10:55] Dana Rousseau: Ok, quick run of the next steps and expectations so procurement can track: pricing, redlines, baseline run, and legal sync. Anything else?
[11:06] Ethan Chen: We also need your sample prompt set, prioritized DPA exceptions, and an initial statement of success for the pilot (latency target, throughput, cost cap).
[11:15] Jonah Lee: We'll send the prompt set and the success criteria doc by EOD 2025-09-12.
[11:21] Hector Alvarez: I'll send DPA exceptions by 2025-09-13.
[11:25] Ethan Chen: Perfect. We'll deliver pricing by Monday, 2025-09-14, and SOC 2 / security binder in the same packet. Riley will start the baseline on 2025-09-16.
[11:34] Marisol Vega: I'll open a JIRA intake for onboarding and share the onboarding checklist.
[11:39] Dana Rousseau: Sounds good. Any competitor-related notes anyone wants to call out?
[11:43] Priya Malhotra: We've been talking to MajorCloudProvider but their latency is worse and pricing higher for EU-bound workloads. Anthropic popped in as well — they have a nice security story but lower throughput.
[11:55] Ethan Chen: Good color — that helps us tailor the pilot.
[11:59] Dana Rousseau: Ok that's it from procurement, thanks everyone.
[12:03] Ethan Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with artifacts.

Recap and commitments (auto):
- Redwood: pricing workbook, SOC 2, DPA/MPF redline checklist, start baseline 2025-09-16.
- Aureon: prompt set and success criteria by 2025-09-12; DPA exception list by 2025-09-13.

End of transcript.
